items.name: Cheddar
items.hook: A firm cow's-milk cheese from the village of Cheddar in Somerset, England.

items.name: Mozzarella
items.hook: A soft, stretchy Italian cheese from Campania, made by stretching curds in hot water.

items.name: Parmesan
items.hook: A hard, granular Italian cheese from Emilia-Romagna, aged at least 12 months and often two to three years.

items.name: Brie
items.hook: A soft, bloomy-rind cow's-milk cheese from the Île-de-France region of France.

items.name: Gouda
items.hook: A Dutch cow's-milk cheese named for the city of Gouda.

items.name: Swiss (Emmental)
items.hook: A firm Swiss cow's-milk cheese from the Emme Valley, famous for its cherry-sized holes, or eyes.

items.name: Provolone
items.hook: A stretched-curd Italian cheese from the south of Italy, aged from a few weeks to over a year.

items.name: Feta
items.hook: A brined Greek cheese made from sheep's milk, sometimes with up to 30 percent goat's milk.

items.name: Gruyère
items.hook: A firm Swiss alpine cheese from the Fribourg region, aged 5 to 12 months or more.

items.name: Comté
items.hook: A firm French alpine cheese from the Jura mountains, made from raw cow's milk and aged from 4 months to over 2 years.

items.name: Manchego
items.hook: A firm Spanish cheese from La Mancha, made only from the milk of Manchega sheep.

items.name: Pecorino Romano
items.hook: A hard, salty Italian grating cheese made from sheep's milk, produced mainly in Sardinia and Lazio.

items.name: Camembert
items.hook: A soft French cheese from Normandy with a white bloomy rind and a creamy, yielding center.

items.name: Gorgonzola
items.hook: An Italian blue cheese from Lombardy, made from cow's milk in two main styles: dolce, soft and sweet, and piccante, firm and sharp.

items.name: Stilton
items.hook: An English blue cheese made only in Derbyshire, Leicestershire, and Nottinghamshire.

items.name: Roquefort
items.hook: A French blue cheese made from sheep's milk and aged in the natural caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

items.name: Asiago
items.hook: An Italian cow's-milk cheese from the Asiago plateau in Veneto.

items.name: Fontina
items.hook: A semi-soft Italian cheese from the Aosta Valley, made from raw cow's milk.

items.name: Taleggio
items.hook: A soft Italian washed-rind cheese from Lombardy, square in shape with a rosy rind and a pale, creamy center.

items.name: Burrata
items.hook: A fresh Italian cheese from Puglia: a pouch of mozzarella filled with stracciatella, shreds of mozzarella soaked in cream.

items.name: Halloumi
items.hook: A firm, brined cheese from Cyprus, traditionally made from sheep and goat milk, now often with cow's milk.

items.name: Paneer
items.hook: A fresh Indian cheese made by curdling hot milk with lemon juice or vinegar, then pressing the curds.

items.name: Queso Fresco
items.hook: A fresh, soft Mexican cheese made from cow's milk, sometimes with goat's milk.

items.name: Cotija
items.hook: An aged Mexican cheese from Michoacán, made from cow's milk.

items.name: Oaxaca Cheese
items.hook: A Mexican stretched-curd cheese from Oaxaca, sold as a ball wound from long ribbons of cheese.

items.name: Havarti
items.hook: A semi-soft Danish cheese with small irregular holes and a smooth, buttery paste.

items.name: Edam
items.hook: A semi-hard Dutch cheese named for the town of Edam, usually sold coated in red wax.

items.name: Monterey Jack
items.hook: A semi-hard American cheese from Monterey County, California.

items.name: Pepper Jack
items.hook: An American cheese made by flavoring Monterey Jack with spicy peppers, usually jalapeño, sometimes habanero and other chiles.

items.name: Colby
items.hook: An American cheese from Wisconsin, made like cheddar but with a washed curd.

items.name: Muenster
items.hook: A semi-soft American deli cheese, pale and smooth with tiny holes and an edible orange rind.

items.name: Raclette
items.hook: A semi-hard Swiss alpine cheese from Valais, made from cow's milk and aged 3 to 6 months.

items.name: Limburger
items.hook: A washed-rind cheese from the Limburg region, now made mostly in Germany and Wisconsin.

items.name: Smoked Gouda
items.hook: A Dutch-style cheese made by smoking young Gouda over hickory or similar wood.

items.name: Jarlsberg
items.hook: A Norwegian cheese with large round holes and a yellow wax rind.

items.name: Salted Butter
items.hook: Churned cream with salt added, at about 80 percent butterfat.

items.name: Unsalted Butter
items.hook: Churned cream with no salt added: the baker's standard butter.

items.name: Cultured Butter
items.hook: Butter churned from fermented cream, in the French and northern European tradition.

items.name: European-Style Butter
items.hook: High-butterfat butter in the European style: 82 to 85 percent fat, less water than standard butter.

items.name: Whipped Butter
items.hook: Butter whipped with air until light and fluffy, sold in tubs.

items.name: Brown Butter
items.hook: Butter cooked until the milk solids toast and turn nutty: the French beurre noisette.

items.name: Ghee
items.hook: Clarified butter from India, simmered longer than standard clarified butter so the solids toast lightly.

items.name: Cream Cheese
items.hook: A soft, fresh, mildly tangy American cheese, spreadable straight from the package.

items.name: Clarified Butter
items.hook: Butter with its water and milk solids removed, leaving clear golden butterfat.

items.name: Compound Butter
items.hook: Softened butter beaten with herbs, aromatics, or sweeteners, then chilled in a log or tub.

items.name: Garlic & Herb Butter
items.hook: A compound butter of butter, garlic, and usually parsley and salt.

items.name: Honey Butter
items.hook: A sweet compound butter of butter whipped with honey and a pinch of salt.

items.name: Cinnamon Butter
items.hook: A sweet compound butter of butter, cinnamon, and sugar, sometimes with a little vanilla.

items.name: Maple Butter
items.hook: A compound butter of butter whipped with maple syrup.

items.name: Lemon Butter
items.hook: A compound butter of butter, lemon juice, and zest.

items.name: Irish Butter
items.hook: Butter made in Ireland from the milk of grass-fed cows, typically cultured and salted, with butterfat around 82 percent.

items.name: Whey Butter
items.hook: Butter churned from the cream that rises on whey left over from cheesemaking.

items.name: Neufchâtel
items.hook: A fresh, soft cheese in the cream cheese family, made with more milk and less cream, so it has about a third less fat.

items.name: Whipped Cream Cheese
items.hook: Cream cheese whipped with air (and sometimes a little milk) into a light, fluffy spread.

items.name: Beurre Blanc
items.hook: A French butter sauce of wine, vinegar, and shallots reduced and whisked with cold butter.

items.name: Whole Milk
items.hook: Fluid milk at its full fat level, about 3.25 percent butterfat.

items.name: 2% Milk
items.hook: Milk with the fat reduced to 2 percent.

items.name: 1% Milk
items.hook: Milk with the fat reduced to 1 percent.

items.name: Skim Milk
items.hook: Milk with nearly all fat removed, under 0.5 percent.

items.name: Chocolate Milk
items.hook: Milk flavored with cocoa and sweetener, usually made from whole or 2% milk.

items.name: Strawberry Milk
items.hook: Milk flavored with strawberry syrup and sweetener, sold ready to drink, usually pink.

items.name: A2 Milk
items.hook: Milk from cows that produce only the A2 form of beta-casein protein, rather than the usual mix of A1 and A2.

items.name: Organic Milk
items.hook: Milk produced under certified organic standards for feed, pasture, and herd care.

items.name: Buttermilk
items.hook: A thick, tangy cultured milk, traditionally the liquid left from butter churning and now made by culturing low-fat milk.

items.name: Half & Half
items.hook: A blend of equal parts milk and cream, with butterfat between about 10.5 and 18 percent.

items.name: Heavy Cream
items.hook: Cream with at least 36 percent butterfat.

items.name: Whipping Cream
items.hook: Cream with about 30 to 36 percent butterfat, formulated to whip.

items.name: Light Cream
items.hook: Cream with about 18 to 30 percent butterfat, between half & half and whipping cream.

items.name: Clotted Cream
items.hook: A thick English cream made by slowly heating cream until it clots into a dense, golden-crusted layer.

items.name: Double Cream
items.hook: A rich British cream with at least 48 percent butterfat, thicker than American heavy cream.

items.name: Evaporated Milk
items.hook: Unsweetened milk concentrated by evaporating about 60 percent of its water, then canned and sterilized.

items.name: Sweetened Condensed Milk
items.hook: Milk concentrated like evaporated milk but with sugar added, making a thick, sweet syrup.

items.name: Powdered Milk
items.hook: Milk dried to a powder, most often nonfat, sometimes whole.

items.name: UHT Milk
items.hook: Milk pasteurized at ultra-high temperature and packed aseptically, so it keeps unopened at room temperature for months.

items.name: Goat Milk
items.hook: Milk from goats, naturally homogenized because its fat globules are small, with a tangy, slightly earthy flavor.

items.name: Sheep Milk
items.hook: Milk from sheep, richer than cow or goat milk in fat, protein, and minerals.

items.name: Eggnog
items.hook: A seasonal dairy drink of milk, cream, egg yolk, sugar, and spices such as nutmeg and cinnamon.

items.name: Malted Milk
items.hook: Milk flavored with malt powder, a blend of malted barley, wheat flour, and milk solids.

items.name: Jersey Milk
items.hook: Milk from Jersey cows, a Channel Islands breed, known for high butterfat and protein.

items.name: Whey
items.hook: The liquid left after milk curdles and the curds are removed in cheesemaking.

items.name: Greek Yogurt
items.hook: Yogurt strained to remove most of its whey, making it thick enough to stand a spoon in, with a dense, tangy taste.

items.name: Skyr
items.hook: An Icelandic strained dairy product made from skim milk, thicker and denser than Greek yogurt, with a very mild tang.

items.name: Plain Yogurt
items.hook: Milk fermented with yogurt cultures into a smooth, tangy gel, sold without added flavors or sweeteners.

items.name: Fruit Yogurt
items.hook: Yogurt sweetened and flavored, most often with fruit preparations, vanilla, or honey.

items.name: Drinkable Yogurt
items.hook: Yogurt made thin enough to drink, sold in bottles, usually flavored and sweetened.

items.name: Kefir
items.hook: A fermented milk drink made with kefir grains, a culture of bacteria and yeasts.

items.name: Cottage Cheese
items.hook: A fresh cheese of loose curds dressed with cream and salt, never pressed or aged.

items.name: Ricotta
items.hook: An Italian fresh cheese traditionally made by recooking whey until its proteins form soft, fine curds.

items.name: Mascarpone
items.hook: An Italian cream cheese from Lombardy, made by curdling cream with acid.

items.name: Quark
items.hook: A fresh German cheese of soured milk, strained to a thick, smooth paste.

items.name: Fromage Blanc
items.hook: A fresh French cheese of curdled milk drained to a soft, spoonable consistency, similar to quark.

items.name: Labneh
items.hook: A Levantine strained yogurt, salted and drained until it reaches a soft cheese consistency.

items.name: Ayran
items.hook: A Turkish savory yogurt drink of yogurt, water, and salt, whisked to a light froth.

items.name: Lassi
items.hook: An Indian yogurt drink blended with water or milk, made sweet, often with mango or rose, or salted and spiced.

items.name: Filmjölk
items.hook: A Swedish cultured milk, mesophilic and mild, with a distinctive pourable, slightly ropy texture.

items.name: Balkan Yogurt
items.hook: A set-style yogurt fermented undisturbed in its container, giving a firm, clean-cut gel and a pronounced tartness.

items.name: Ryazhenka
items.hook: A cultured milk from Eastern Europe made from baked milk: milk held at low heat for hours until creamy and caramel-tinted, then fermented.

items.name: Smetana
items.hook: The sour cream of Central and Eastern Europe, cultured cream with a clean tang and a thick, spoonable body, usually around 20 to 30 percent fat in commercial versions.

items.name: Sour Cream
items.hook: Cream cultured until it thickens and turns pleasantly tart.

items.name: Crème Fraîche
items.hook: A French cultured cream, thick and velvety with a mild, nutty tang, around 30 to 45 percent fat.

items.name: Vanilla
items.hook: The classic ice cream flavor, made with real vanilla or vanilla extract.

items.name: Chocolate
items.hook: Ice cream flavored with cocoa or chocolate: one of the two oldest ice cream flavors and a permanent fixture in the top three sellers.

items.name: Strawberry
items.hook: Sweet cream ice cream flavored with real strawberries or strawberry puree.

items.name: Cookies & Cream
items.hook: Vanilla ice cream loaded with crushed chocolate sandwich cookie pieces.

items.name: Mint Chocolate Chip
items.hook: Cool mint ice cream studded with chocolate pieces, often tinted pale green.

items.name: Cookie Dough
items.hook: Vanilla ice cream filled with chunks of chocolate chip cookie dough, usually with chocolate chips of its own.

items.name: Butter Pecan
items.hook: Vanilla or brown-sugar ice cream filled with butter-roasted pecans.

items.name: Rocky Road
items.hook: Chocolate ice cream with marshmallow and nuts, born in Oakland, California in 1929.

items.name: Neapolitan
items.hook: A tri-flavor ice cream sold in one carton, classically chocolate, vanilla, and strawberry in three distinct bands.

items.name: French Vanilla
items.hook: A premium vanilla ice cream made from a cooked egg-yolk custard base, rather than plain sweet cream.

items.name: Coffee
items.hook: An ice cream flavored with coffee, ranging from lightly tan and sweet to dark and intense.

items.name: Pistachio
items.hook: An ice cream flavored with pistachio paste and dotted with nut pieces.

items.name: Salted Caramel
items.hook: An ice cream of caramel-flavored base with ribbons of salted caramel sauce.

items.name: Moose Tracks
items.hook: A licensed American flavor: vanilla ice cream with peanut butter cups and a thick fudge ribbon.

items.name: Black Cherry
items.hook: An almond-scented or vanilla base studded with dark, tart black cherries.

items.name: Rum Raisin
items.hook: An ice cream flavored with rum and studded with rum-soaked raisins.

items.name: Butter Brickle
items.hook: A butter-flavored ice cream with pieces of butter brickle candy, a toffee of butter and brown sugar.

items.name: Spumoni
items.hook: A molded Italian-style dessert of layered ice creams, classically chocolate, cherry, and pistachio, with candied fruit and nuts.

items.name: Sherbet
items.hook: A frozen dessert of fruit juice or purée with a little milk, between sorbet and ice cream in richness.

items.name: Sorbet
items.hook: A frozen dessert of sweetened fruit juice or purée and water, with no dairy.

items.name: Gelato
items.hook: An Italian frozen dessert churned denser and served warmer than ice cream, with less air and usually less fat.

items.name: Frozen Yogurt
items.hook: A frozen dessert of yogurt and milk, sold in hard-packed pints and soft-serve shops.

items.name: Soft Serve
items.hook: A frozen dairy dessert served directly from a machine that freezes and aerates the mix at once.

items.name: Kulfi
items.hook: An Indian frozen dessert of milk reduced by slow simmering until thick, sweetened and flavored (cardamom, saffron, pistachio), then frozen dense in molds.

items.name: Mochi Ice Cream
items.hook: Bite-sized balls of ice cream wrapped in sweet rice dough (mochi).
